Federation is a strategy game, created by Gordon Miller that takes place in space. There are lots of different options and it is quite difficult. For advanced players only... 
 
The Galactic Federation welcomes you to the finest army in the galaxy. As a new recruit you will receive a brand new starship, 35000 cash advance and a lifetime of adventure.

214924.overview: A sequel to Gordon Miller's Federation, like the original Federation game, this is a strategy game, created by Gordon Miller that takes place in space. There are lots of different options and it is quite difficult. For advanced players only... The Galactic Federation welcomes you to the finest army in the galaxy. As a new recruit you will receive a brand new starship, 35000 cash advance and a lifetime of adventure.

215010.overview:
An Italian game created by Marco Caricati in the style of the famous puzzle-game Columns, but introducing some variations that force the player to make a major strategic commitment, which will make things more frenetic and exciting in this test of skill, timing and chance.   The game is structured in 30 stages, in which you will have to use tactics and intelligence to fix blocks of colored gems falling from above. The aim is to build horizontal, vertical and diagonal lines formed by at least three diamonds of the same color: once built, these lines are eliminated from the playing area leaving it free space they previously occupied. The "target" to be reached is different for each level and comes briefly described at each stage change: single gems, horizontal lines, vertical, diagonal, "stars" and "target pieces". Target pieces are drawn with an exclamation point ! and must be eliminated to finish the stage.  
 
  There are some special colored tokens that can be used at same way of gems; forming rows with pawns and diamonds of the same color will have different effects depending on the meaning

215011.overview: An update to the Anco Software Gridstart super series racing grand prix game from Bug + Steeler Norway with 6 tracks to choose from. Grid Start 3 is a Formula 1 racing game played from a third person perspective similar to Pole Position. The game consists of six tracks based on real world locations. These can be played in a competition consisting of three laps or in a practice mode with 99 laps (or until the player presses the escape key). In each race there are 23 AI controlled cars to compete against. The game is playable in three difficulties: novice, amateur and professional. The car has six gears that have to be changed manually and a boost feature can also be used for faster acceleration. In addition to racing faster than the opposing drivers the player also has to avoid crashing into the haystacks and the fences that are placed dangerously close to the track.

215012.overview: A great looking platform shooter demo with the feel of Sonic the Hedgehog, with added firepower. It was created by the masterminds at Oracle Design and released for play in 1994.

215043.overview: A from scratch homebrew version of Alien Storm in AMOS. To compensate for AMOS' famous slowness it was downsized to a portion of the screen as though it were being played on a Game Gear handheld, which resolved much of the slowness and scrolling issues. It remains in an unfinished but playable state up to the Gilling Monster.

215044.overview: An Amiga port of the popular arcade game by Sunteam in the style of GameGear ESWAT. Just as in the original ...crime is getting out of control in Liberty City, and to combat the problem, the LCPD establishes a new unit, called ESWAT (Enhanced Special Weapons and Tactics). Police officers who are promoted to this unit wear a cyber-suit that contains state-of-the-art military equipment including two Turbo-Booster Thrusters, extra ammunition, and increased protection. In order to become an ESWAT member, all a dedicated police officer has to do is arrest enough criminal masterminds to progress through the ranks, which include Captain, Assistant Chief, and Chief.

215068.overview:
Gloom MOD for the Amiga created by Gareth Murfin aka Alpha aka Zombie Massacre "Gloom4". Both 2 player co-op mode and 2 player combat mode are also available. In each level, your objective is to find an exit before your 3 lives run out. In specific levels, you must defeat (or escape) enemy bosses. The zombies are back in a standalone game. Zombie Massacre uses the Gloom Deluxe engine to create a first person shooter in a horror setting.
Gloom’s engine can throw a lot of enemy sprites at the player, so hordes of zombies are appropriate adversaries.

215069.overview: 8bit Killer is an indie game first-person 3D shooter that was initially released for Microsoft Windows in 2008 it was later ported to Amiga in 2014. It plays like early raycasting games such as Catabomb 3D or Wolfenstein 3D, featuring music and aesthetics one may find in an 8bit game for the Nintendo Entertainment System. This is an Amiga port of sorts in the Gloom engine. Textures and some sounds were reused. However, the story screens and the music were removed. Due to engine limitations, none of the original levels were recreated.

215070.overview: Mod for Gloom for both Amiga and AmigaCD32. Both 2 player co-op mode and 2 player combat mode are also available.  In each level, your objective is to find an exit before your 3 lives run out. In specific levels, you must defeat (or escape) enemy bosses.

215072.overview: A two player Gloom Mod using elements from Final Fantasy X created by nittamituaki and released in2014. In each level, your objective is to find an exit before your 3 lives run out. In specific levels, you must defeat (or escape) enemy bosses. It features cooperative 2 player gaming. Blood options can be set to level of comfort, including Meaty/Nasty Mode where enemy larvae explode more violently but disappear quickly and Messy/Dirty Mode where all larvae of defeated enemies will remain on the ground where they died until the level is completed.

215073.overview: Gloom was written in Blitz Basic by Mark Sably. The game displays 64 colors in ECS/RTG. The game uses the Gloom 2 (deluxe) engine. Special version of Gloom. Some graphics have been changed/improved. In each level, your objective is to find an exit before your 3 lives run out. In specific levels, you must defeat (or escape) enemy bosses. Features one and two player modes.

215074.overview:
Did IT Come From the Desert? is a first-person shooter inspired by Cinemaware's Mega Drive version of It Came from the Desert.

The game contains 18 levels divided over five episodes with different settings. There are five standard enemy types like green ants and antheads, and two boss enemies, the King Ant and the Queen Ant. All enemies can attack in melee range, and some can also attack from distance. The player can defend themselves with a flame thrower, which can be upgraded to a plasma gun in later levels. There are some extra items for restoring the player's health, keys to unlock doors, an item to make the player invisible for a short amount of time and coins which can be used to buy useful stuff in the shop.

The game is implemented as a total conversion of Gloom 3's game engine

215076.overview: The first age of MODs for Gloom. In each level, your objective is to find an exit before your 3 lives run out. In specific levels, you must defeat (or escape) enemy bosses.

215079.overview: This MOD is for 1 player game. 2 player mode is not available. In each level, your objective is to find an exit before your 3 lives run out. In specific levels, you must defeat (or escape) enemy bosses.

215081.overview: You were at a loss at what to do next. Just then an old man started talking to you. "Spekkio is the god of battle. Try your strength. You have all the time in the world!" In each level, your objective is to find an exit before your 3 lives run out. In specific levels, you must defeat (or escape) enemy bosses.

215082.overview: A set of Mods for Gloom entitled either Gloom Mod Map or Plenty of New Maps, which is just that with content from nittamituaki, AmigaFans, FirstAge, Plenty1, Plenty2, Plenty3 and a IDO-CD32 compilation.

215086.overview: The 2014 remake (by Czeslaw Mnich and Amigafans in the Gloom Engine) of the one of the original Doom style games that was made for the Amiga by Apache Software in 1995. This first person shooter was something like a first-person version of Into the Eagle's Nest. This version chose to do away with the split screen and focus on the core of the game. Co-operative multi-player is available.

215093.overview:
A two player gravity combat game by Sami-Pekka Haavisto aka Queer of Clones. G-Rocker 0.97 is beta version of TurboRaketti-style two player combat game, where players control little vessels trying to wipe the opponent out. Though the game is beta version, it is fully playable and has (almost) all features final version should have had. Only thing missing are original music, more and better graphics, more scene types and couple of new weapons.
 The game may seem a pretty one-to-one copy of TurboRaketti, but I can assure you it is quite different. The main thing is playability, and I think this
 is the best game in it's genre that works with old A500 (with 1MB memory). There may never be final version, since nowadays I code for PC, but if I get
 nasty bug reports, I may fix the game a little. By the way, I'm currently working on PC-version of G-Rocker, and it will appear to funet as soon as
 it gets somewhere.

215115.overview: A 2D arcade adventure/puzzle game created with AMOS by Mark Judge and released as Shareware in 1994. It is in the style of Prince of Persia.

215153.overview: A collect & avoid style game created in AMOS which is based on the game stylings of Oil's Well.  Written in AMOS Professional. Coding & graphics by Paul ''ExiE'' Strejcek and Johny/Vectors. Music by unknown author. Game includes a level editor allowing players to create their own levels. The player mines gold from the underground using a special mining device, while having to watch out for various creatures that get in the way.

215165.overview: A remake of a Nintendo Game and Watch, two screen game for the Amiga platform, created by Mike Verstaevel and released on an unsuspecting world in 1998.  Keep all your precious plants well hydrated.

215166.overview: A Formula 1 racing and management game created in AMOS by Ave Avid and released in 1993 by 17 Bit Software. Choose your engine, gather and pay your team, get sponsorship and keep enough money rolling in to keep you rolling across the finish line.

215234.overview: A Go board game recreation by O Forster and released in 1990.

215318.overview: This unreleased platform game by Michael Häbich and Daniel Amend was found in a preview spread to the BBSes in summer of 1996.

215320.overview: Eric and the Floaters was the release title for the European port of Bomberman on MSX and ZX Spectrum in 1983. This game, however, doesn't play quite like the famous classic. You do have to blow up monsters, but they can't harm you. Instead, you lose a life when you used the last of the 20 bombs you get at the start of the game, or if you get hit by your own bomb blast. One of the monsters in each level is randomly given the key that you need to progress to next level. Originally released professionally as a £9.99 title, it was later changed to public domain.

217485.overview: A one or two player shooter written exclusively for use with the Golem light gun. GATEWAY Y was sold as part of the retail Golem light gun package.

219293.overview: A Slavic language puzzle game created by Sva prava zadržana of 32Bita and published by 32Bita in 1994.

219297.overview: A single player public domain game inspired by the PD game Highspeed.

219754.overview: Behind the weighty name hides more of a David of the tinkering genre: Two players (a weak computer opponent can step in if desired) try to put together randomly given figures on a 16 x 16 field board to form rectangles. Practically and in terms of rules, this amounts to something like a mixture of "Tetris" and "Reversi". The story is spiced up a little by two additional game modes with bonus stones or other game field limitations, a help function and various character sets Despite the stone-typical compulsion to repeat, also known as the addictive effect.

417668.overview: A puzzle game created by Martin Auer and released in 1990 in OASE No. 126.

418268.overview: A difficult Maze War adventure game variant, with only 2 predefined maps, but includes a map editor. Released as PD.

418314.overview: Port of the Linux strategy game Konquest. Requires an Amiga with Kickstart 3.0+. The goal is to control all 20 planets on the map. Planets produce one of 4 types of battle starships. The stronger your fleet, the more likely you can advance in your progress to conquer the galaxy.

418389.overview: A Cute'em-up made with SEUCK and released to the public domain by Fun Club in 1991.

418400.overview: A Tetris game featuring many backgrounds and piece tile sets to offer a wide variety of play. The graphics change with each level.

418605.overview: The INNOVATIVE 10 out of 10 Series. These highly acclaimed suites of programs are a revolutionary step forward in educational software. They ALL use a unique system of automatically recording children's progress as they play and learn. This is just one of the many features which sets the 10 out of 10 Series in a class of its own. Each package contains SIX expertly designed educational games covering TEN essential areas of a child's education. All packages cover a wide age range and subjects are available for all children from three to sixteen years of age. As children learn from the games their progress is automatically recorded in 36 Y specific challenges the National Curriculum Attainment Targets of these areas are optionally displayed on screen in subject-based packages. All the programs are designed in Britain to be fun for single players or groups and the assessment system can monitor the progress of up to 4000 children with no input from parent or teacher needed. Watch them, join in the fun or leave them and return later to check their progress. You're in control! For ages 8 to 18! Contains words, phrases, sentences, grammar, shopping, school, the family, travel, health and sports.

419285.overview: This is a transcode from the original arcade game Z80 to 68K assembly.

420721.overview: A Game & Watch style Goonies inspired action game.

420914.overview:
A possibly unfinished game intended to be shareware, created by Arno Duwe. The year is 3001 and the Earth has been tyrannized for 4 millennia by Ronalds from the 5th dimension. You, the last hope of the earthlings, stand read for the mission. Take Geoffrey and move around the screen, picking up all the yellow marbles and then move him to the green section safely, avoiding the fire. 
- the game has 31 levels
- choose either music or sounds
- once per level you can press fire = Geoffrey runs faster and for this time all aliens get knocked out
- the green field (square) is a pause field (square)
- the red field (square) opens the door if all stones have been collected
- each 5th level has only one devil - after finishing it you get one extra life
- in this demo-version you can play levels 1, 9, 15, 19, 20 (no matter if you failed one or passed it)
- push the fire-button

420966.overview: A shareware action game from the Backyard Brothers in 1997. Each level is set on a pond of some sort with stones that tend to dip under the water. The idea is to collect 10 coins to complete a level.

420990.overview: You star as Godzilla, and your mission is to shoot everything what moves, Houses and other Enemies which will attempt to kill you

421042.overview: The Griffon Legend is a freeware zelda-like RPG created in FreeBASIC as part of a contest by Syn9 (Daniel Kennedy). 500 years after the Griffon-Dragon war, the Dragons have returned to reclaim their empire. Cities are falling, everyone is dying, and the lone Griffon Knight Fayne is caught up in the middle of it all.

421045.overview: A Castlevania inspired gothic beat-em up created using Earok's excellent Scorpion Engine. Use your sword to dispatch the unholy undead and creatures of the night.

421254.overview: A homebrew golf game from the Beyond Arts team of Dinko Nazor, Dobrica Pavlinusic and Damir Bulic. The AGA version is finished and there is also an unfinished non-AGA version.

421275.overview: GNU Robbo is a free open source reimplementation of Janusz Pelc’s Robbo  for the Atari XE/XL which was distributed by LK Avalon  in 1989.

422045.overview: A side scrolling shooting game by John Dondzila, from 1990, in which you shoot various pieces of food!

422046.overview: Take part as a ghost in this mine game! A Boulder Dash-like action puzzle game for one person from Wily E. and released to PD in 1993.

422048.overview:
A game in which you manage a trucking company in Germany. First published commercially in 1992 by OASE, updated versions of GERMAN TRUCKING (sans printed manual) were subsequently released as shareware in 1993/94 by developers DGM-Software.
Known releases:
- V1.0 (1992)
- V2.0 (1993/94)
- V2.1 (22-Sep-94)

422074.overview: A SEUCK-based space shooter released as shareware in 1990 by Aidan Palmer.

422075.overview: A  shareware space strategy game circa 1993.

422086.overview: A single player boulder dash style action puzzle created by Marcus Strauss in 1993. Released on Assassins PD 141 along with Black Dawn and Reversi II.

422087.overview: Collection of 6 classic computer games: Croak, Mouthman, D1-planes, Drip, Jump'n roll , Squamble

422090.overview:
A shareware text adventure created by Jim MacBrayne and published in 1989. Jim has obviously been strongly influenced by Infocom when writing The Golden Fleece, relying on a good storyline and atmospheric descriptions, not to mention intricate puzzles! I would have preferred a few more easy puzzles dotted about the game to make me feel I was achieving more in the early stages, rather than spending a lot of time exploring and mapping but otherwise making little progress. 
 
Zeus has challenged his son, the messenger god Hermes, with finding a mortal man capable of locating and acquiring of the legendary Golden Fleece. You are that man.

422093.overview: In this game freeware action game you have to collect various pieces of fruit whilst avoiding monsters.

422097.overview: A surreal AMOS based shareware game created by Overdose Software and released in 1992. A two player claymation style shoot out game. First one to draw and hit twice wins! Fire by pressing the required key after the Draw! sound effect. Player 1 uses Space Bar, Player 2 uses Enter\Return Key. Pressing early will lock up your gun.

422101.overview:
A shareware text adventure by Phil Richmond with music by D. J. Nuthall, written using Creative Adventure Toolkit in 1994. In this game you take on the role of Archibald Blake, retired Bank Clerk, fitness fanatic and lepidopterist. Blake has started on a short hiking vacation and is set for a very strange adventure.... NOW PLAY ON... 
 
Game was part of a series of games including Hazardous Holiday, Piggery Jokery, and Paranormal Palace.

422104.overview: Appears to be some kind of RTS/board game. WARNING: The terrain is full of robots.

422106.overview: German language eco-adventure by Digighost Game Design where the goal is saving the environment. The foreground is. The player must fight against the take on “gray power” and revive diseased trees, detoxify waterways and remove garbage. In addition to the detailed graphics, the... players are also offered sound effects.

422111.overview: A Worm\Tron style lightcycles game for 2 or more players, includes tournament rules for more players. Published in Assassins CD2 Ultimate Games 95.

422121.overview: A text and picture based adventure game from Bob Hand in 1992.

422315.overview: An Amiga OCS port of the FM7/PC88 version of this game which was first ported to the X68000 by Beauty Planets. This new Amiga game is by hitchhikr SoftWorks. A game in which you need to destroy as many waves as possible to get the best of hiscores.

422426.overview: This Asteroids clone from author, Adam Girvin presents itself without any great backstory or other frills. Your The mission is simple: Destroy all flying items and enemies! Well, if that's all! Save the Earth by destroying all the invading Greeblies to clear a path to the final confrontation with the Greeblie King!  Written in Blitz Basic 2 v1.6

422600.overview: An educational program, checking geographic knowledge about the world. It features an extensive educational part based on the attached maps.

422738.overview: Control the Golem that you beamed down to the hostile planet where systems are not working properly. Solve the puzzles to move around and investigate the issues to find success were the goals in this unreleased Underground Software game from 1997.

422810.overview: Presented before you is a string of Lemmings, click the button and they fart in the face of the one behind them. This game was the 1994 equivalent of being Rickrolled. You spent time downloading this game and in the end got a face full of stink. Then, because you needed to keep your upload\download ratio up, you shared it and passed on the stink to someone else. There were several sequels to this game.

422812.overview: An avoid-it style arcade game, move your chosen creature up the vertically scrolling aisle without bumping into anyone. Firing the button throws a cake. Released for Christmas 1995.

422813.overview: A Christmas treat of a game. Help Santa deliver all the packages.

423035.overview: Compete to conquer the galaxy. You start on a home planet and a certain amount of ships. Each turn, the fleet or parts of it can be moved. Traveling to other worlds takes time, and reaching distant worlds may take several rounds. During each round, random events may happen, from pirate attacks or natural disasters, affecting one or more players and fleets. If a fleet is approaching a world defended by another fleet, a fight takes place without interaction: there is a random element involved, but generally the player with the bigger fleet wins.

423037.overview: An unfinished first person role playing game from Blob in 1990. Move around the dungeon, mapping as you go and fight the denizens you find there.

423355.overview: A freeware soccer management simulation created by Stefan Schwartz of Black Soft in 1989. Contains players and teams from the 1989/1990 season.

423372.overview:
A game made to look and play much like Ghostbusters, created by Andrews Heckles and published by F1 Licenseware. go out and "bust" the spectral hauntings that are occurring all over the city. You do this through the use of nuclear-accelerated "proton packs" and "ghost traps", whereby the ghosts can be captured and transferred to a secure storage facility at their Headquarters. However New York City has suddenly become a very haunted place, and the number of ghosts has suddenly and dramatically increased. The Ghostslayers must reduce the paranormal psychokinetic energy, the "PK level" in the city, which represents ghost power.  
 
An action game that features an overhead-view and a side-view. From Ghostslayers HQ, the player must monitor a map of midtown Manhattan for "ghost alarms", as well as for casual, roaming spirits, and plot a route to the alarmed area. Once the route is plotted, the player then controls the purchased Ghostslayermobile as it drives through traffic. Here, the player is able to capture casual ghosts on the way if they are en route.

423450.overview: An AMOS based golf score application from Ross Cleary  to allow you to track and better understand your scores and where you can improve.

423466.overview: An AMOS based automobile racing management simulator made by Ave Avid in 1992. More a management and strategy game than a racing game, despite the name.

423476.overview: If you are into golf in the sense of playing the sport, then consider this disk, as it will keep accurate records of your courses as well as your current handicap.  Excellently produced using AMOS. Created by Peter Wilson and published by 17-Bit Software and as shareware in 1990.

423493.overview: An Italian language SIMON style freeware game from Cris in 1987. You play the demon in hell, poking the Grilli in the bum to get them to repeat the code\song as it was previously given. Listen to the sequence with which the 4 crickets sing. Then poke them so that they sing in the same way and they will gradually add an extra note.

423517.overview: A shareware card, casino game created by Rolf "Pattex" Noch in 1997. A game which made it very simple to create your own cards from images with the registered versions.

423632.overview:
A Polish language educational game intended for primary school students who learn from scratch to recognize parts of speech, their inflections by cases and by pages. After starting, a menu appears on the screen from which you can select the material you are interested in. These sections are intended for grades 1-3, 4-6, 7-8. Selecting the first two parts of the material results in the exclusion of certain topics (the idea is that the material in the program corresponds to what is taught at school). Before you start learning, you can also turn on some music to accompany you while you sew. After selecting the material, we can read lectures on this topic or go straight to the exercises. 
 
Lectures:This part is divided into 4 topics: inflected parts of speech, indeclinable parts of speech, conjugation and declamation. The first topic contains information about verbs, nouns, adjectives, numerals and pronouns. The second one contains information about adverbs, adverbial pronouns, prepositions, conjunctions, exclamations and particles. All topics covered by these lectures are presented in text form and constitute information that can be found in most Polish grammar textbooks.

Exercises:The exercises are divided into two parts: conjugation of words and definition 
Grammar tutor: part of speech. In the first case, a word appears on the screen and must either be inflected by parts (active, passive, reflexive) or by cases (nominative, genitive, dative, accusative, instrumental, locative). The learner's task is to fill in the appropriate fields. correct forms of words. Note - once a word has been entered (confirmed with Enter), it cannot be corrected! After entering all the forms, the computer uses the symbols + ico to determine what has been done well and what has been done poorly, and also informs us whether we have coped with the given task. To make it more difficult when declinating by cases, the given word should also be declined either in number, plural or singular and so forth.

423792.overview: A polish language learning software program.  Learn how to solve mathematical tasks - all based on computer animations. Teach yourself everything about geometry, learning all the theorems, methods of solving tasks, all based on examples, using informative computer animation.

423861.overview: A Polish-language geometry learning program from Tomasz Liasta with music by Karol Pieruta and published by Fasterbit in 1994.

423877.overview: GEOMETRIA STRUCTURE II - NEW planimetry - patterns, tasks, lectures also based on computer animation. Learn all about Geometry in Polish released by Alderan in 1993.

423931.overview: An unfinished 1989 frog platformer originally created for commercial release by Michael Pollard and Alan Burns and demoed to Creative Edge, who loved it and hired them on. The game was designed to complete with the likes of Zool and B.O.B, with a slick main character and very fast paced action throughout. The aim though was to try and surpass both of its inspirations and create something to completely blow Amiga users away. Not long after signing up the game, David reveals a deal was made with Atari to make the game an exclusive for the Jaguar. Sadly this would signify the end of the Amiga development, and there not been the exclusivity – it would have been finished and released on the Amiga.

423986.overview: Literally "Gallows Bird" in German, this is a German language hangman word puzzle game where you try to guess the word or phrase before you swing fully from a rope.

423996.overview: A four player German language version of Wheel of Fortune game created by Hari Wiguna in 1989.

424286.overview: Intended to be a very Doom-like experience to the Amiga including a  brand new HUD and protagonist, which are gonna replace the old Free-Doom placeholder that were in use during the testing phase of game design. The final version draws heavy inspirations from Steampunk and Lovecraftian themes. The project is still considered a work in progress. Pickup your time machine and travel back, dive into an alternative universe where Doom was never released for PCs in 1993, but several years earlier on the humble Amiga 500! Grind is a new fps game powered by the amazing Dread engine: a mind-blowing achievement which showcases what was really possible with Amiga's original hardware!

424864.overview:
Grand Ouvert is German language Skat cards game simulation, released commercially in 1989. Now you can play your AMIGA according to all the rules of the art of "Schneider Schwarz". Grand Overt adheres strictly to the official rules. Authored by Manfred Leidorf and Steffen Hantschel with the first version released in 1989 and the last, version 4.1 in 1992.  
 
Grand Overt masters all the rules and ways of playing. With a graphically perfectly styled user interface, Grand Overt immediately conveys a "regulars' table atmosphere". The game is mouse-controlled, easy to use and completely in German. Grand Overt strictly adheres to the official rules of the game and promises long-lasting motivation.

424868.overview:
The Ghosts of Blackwood Manor is an award-winning interactive horror from Stefan Vogt, the acclaimed author of Hibernated and The Curse of Rabenstein. 
 
Take on the role of novelist Thomas King and his wife Cora as they move into a remote Scottish manor house, just days before Christmas 1986. Seeking inspiration for his next book, Thomas begins to explore the history of Blackwood Manor, only to uncover a dark secret that dates back centuries to the days of the Great Scottish Witch Hunts.

The Ghosts of Blackwood Manor is a complex interactive fiction piece written in Infocom's advanced Z-machine format XZIP. The game has three different endings, a bad, a neutral and a good ending, depending on the player's choices. It is very likely that the player, on a first playthrough, will not reach the good ending, even though it is possible. Reaching the bad or neutral ending first is part of the experience and helps the player understanding the true intentions of some of the NPCs and the impact of decisions made, so they may be reconsidered.

444319.overview: Created for the  Revision 2024 demo party and created with ASM 68k by Oxygene, this logic puzzle game has excellent graphics and brain scratching difficulty. In it, you can only move colored blobs left or right by using the two mouse buttons. The goal is to glue all same color blogs together, which will make them happy.  If you manage to glue two blobs horizontally another color can use it as a bridge. If you make a wrong move click retry. Has level codes and at least 20 levels at current count.

447007.overview: In the 70s and 80s video poker machines were very popular where the player does not play against a human opponent but rather plays against the computer.

447021.overview: Battaglia Navale is a very popular pencil and paper game all over the world.

447076.overview: A classic game of mines. The playing field is a rectangular field made up of many small squares. The aim of the game is to uncover all the squares by clicking on them while avoiding mines. The squares containing the mines will explode and end the game. When a square is uncovered it can happen that a number appears ranging from 1 to 8 indicating the number of adjacent squares that contain mines. If, however, none of the adjacent squares contain mines, they will come automatically discovered. A freeware puzzle game from Giovanni Iacobelli in 2021.

447152.overview: GI Puzzle Balls is a Columns clone developed by Giovanni Iacobelli and released into the public domain in 2021.

448127.overview: Gox! is a 3 reel slot machine emulator created by Dutch programer  Etienne Koreman in 1995, with three main revisions, each with a different style of reels, all came out that year.

448605.overview:
This is a transcode from the original arcade game Z80 to 68K assembly.

Game description:

Galaga is a vertical arcade shooter from Namco. You control a space fighter at the bottom of the screen, scrolling left and right in order to avoid oncoming bombs and kamikaze attacks from alien invaders--and to fire your own missiles to fight back!

There are an infinite number of stages to progress through. Every third level is a "challenge stage" in which you have a free chance to shoot as many aliens as possible and rack up bonus points.

Certain aliens have tractor beams they can use to capture one of your ships. If that wasn't your last "life," you can try to shoot that alien down and recapture your ship, giving you two ships at once and doubling your firepower.

A summary screen appears when the game is over, giving you both your final score and your final "hit ratio"--the number of missiles fired, enemies destroyed, and the percentage of targets hit.

The Amiga version is a source code conversion of the original arcade.

448697.overview: Step into the breathtaking world of The Grid and dive into an action-packed race like no other! Mount your futuristic light-bike and enter the grid where strategy and reflexes determine victory or defeat.

449066.overview: A compilation of four games from Courbois Software in 1989. Games include: Insluitertje, Alle Negen, Checkers and a worm game called Target.

449085.overview: A compilation of four games from Courbois Software in 1989. Games include Yathzee, Power Poker, Simon and Mastermind.

449087.overview: A compilation of four games from Courbois Software in 1989. Games include: Acht Op Een Rij, Olie Magnaat, Duizende and Domino.

449146.overview: A billiards like game for one or two players is included on Amiga Spiele 1 and Amiga Extra 3.  BLIFF is a mixture of billiards and golf. Alone or with another player, the aim is to get balls the pool table after a carom. The only thing that can disturb your concentration is the computer fan...

449696.overview:
Galactic Miners is a single player, commercial adventure\edutainment game, developed and published by Rush Software and written with CanDo, which was released in Australia in 1992. The coding team was Greg Abernethy and Martin Fitzgibbons.  
 
The story is that you are returning from an expedition to the mining colonies of Tauran when you encounter an unexpected asteroid shower. Your ship, the Flying Kangaroo, is damaged but you were able to manage to land safely on a nearby planet. You find damage to your fuel storage tanks and your communications systems. You are stranded unless you can find enough raw materials to produce fuel and repairs for your ship. Using your short range shuttle and your Scorpion Mine Probe, you investigate the potential mining locations scattered around the planet. You will need to safely navigate around the planet, evaluate each site and steer the scorpion through the underground spaces to obtain the minerals and produce fuel. Your handy tools will guide you through the planning. You had better get started food, water and other necessities will necessitate that you hurry, so get to the bridge!

449789.overview:
Garden is a 1-player arcade game. 

The player controls a small character, who attempts to pick flowers from a public garden while avoiding a guard. Played from a top-down perspective, the guard runs unwaveringly towards the player, but can only follow the player along the path they make in the grass. The guard, whose job is to protect the garden, will not trample the grass himself. When the player has picked all flowers, they proceed to the next similar challenge. Several obstacles in the garden serve to complicate the flower picking. The player only has a single life, and it is game over if they are caught.

449793.overview: The Guardian 3 Geyer' s Final Strike

449800.overview: A remake\reworking of the Galaga game for the Amiga 2000, the final version of the game was released in 2001, but the initial full version came out in 2000, hence the name. Darkside PD (John Snowball) was the creator of this freeware interpretation. Galaga 2000 (ver 2.0) is a 40 level single screen shoot 'em up with may more intricate power ups than the original. You control a space fighter at the bottom of the screen, scrolling left and right in order to avoid oncoming bombs and kamikaze attacks from alien invaders--and to fire your own missiles to fight back!

449801.overview: A homebrew shooter by Stuart Ashen of Dancing Yak Productions in 1995. In the game you get to name them after your worst enemy in the world. Select the manner of their execution and watch the trial and execution. A secret word can be typed in the Secret menu to get some hidden content. There are 10 methods of execution to vent your spleen with or you can choose a random method.

449815.overview:
A very laudable clone of an old game called Infection. You and another player attempt to cover a board in counters
of your own color by placing your counters either side of the opponent's counters (vertical, diagonal or horizontal, by the way) and thereby turning his/her counters to your color. Originally Ian Davison designed this as a two -player-only game but wisely decided to include the single-player mode. Once you've discovered how to turn on the automatic mode , so that you don 't have to work out which counters to keep turning over all the time, it's a lot of fun.

Ian's even included a challenge mode which then allows the player to go through a series of preset grids. Great stuff
indeed. Ian admits that the computer 's Al is a little predictable, and that's about the only thing that 's really wrong with the game - you can set up traps very easily and the computer will often walk straight into them .

449816.overview: A Boulderdash\Emerald Mine game created by Skippy and published to both the Emerald Mines Club Australia and Emerald Mine Club Holland in 1993. 80 caves to explore. This is the second and final game in this series, however Skippy had dozens of releases in about a 7 year period in the 90's.

450092.overview: Gunslinger is a 1-2 player wild west themed run and gun style shooter developed by Stew Perkins using the Shoot 'Em Up Construction Kit, and released into the public domain in 1992.

450120.overview: A bird's eye action reflex game by Andreas Neumann and Daniel Radel of Nuedelsoft, released as freeware in 1992. Grab the space-faring flies as quick as you can!

450231.overview: A Pascal based puzzle game created by Markus Illenseer, with version 1.0 being released 3.9.1991. Game comes with a level loader where you can generate your own levels by using an ASCII-editor to modify the 14x14 GetemLevels file. The Gadget Score will show the score on your last 10 levels. Sound implemented without slowing game play appreciably. Find the matching pieces. Pieces falling down to a floor when moved over free space. This is a completely new idea and has nothing in common with Tetris or Shanghai. Controlled by mouse or keyboard.

450309.overview: Guide your Psycho Ninja Gobbit (frog?) over all the squares to change their color, avoiding bumping into the "baddies" of course. You begin on a pyramid, and you get a different shape on every level. Your joystick prowess will be tested in this very well presented game with good graphics and music. This AMOS based freeware game from 1990 is often found packaged with  PONTOON.

450484.overview: Geografia Polski v1.0 is an educational program, checking geographic knowledge about Poland. It features an extensive educational part based on the attached maps and a test with 5 levels of difficulty. The test consists of 20 questions. Each question has a map and 3 options to choose from. After the test is completed, the final result is displayed.

451826.overview: An AMOS based shareware platform game published by Nathan Wolf in 1998. Help Al the alligator save his kidnapped mother, fight a horde of henchmen from your arch rival, Jellyroll. While you are on your way you can grab all the gems you can find.

451858.overview: A shareware action\worm game from Pete Kerckhoff, with version 1.6 created in 1988. A "snake" game written in compiled AmigaBASIC with a few unusual touches. When the worm eats the subterranean strawberries, it grows, and a rock appears on the screen. But colliding with a rock (rocks are optional) doesn't kill the worm, it only cuts it a segment shorter. Colliding with walls is also non-lethal, only stopping the worm in its tracks. However, colliding itself will kill the worm. Released in AUGS disk #13 (v1.6).

451999.overview:
Based on Udo Reiss's Commercial game, published by Kingsoft, this freeware reworking of the classic single screen shooter was done four years later by ICE in 1993 and was available on Spielekiste Nr. 388. Like the original, this was a Galaga clone. The player controls a spaceship that can only move left and right at the bottom of the screen. The aim of the game is to destroy as many enemy waves as possible without losing all of the extra lives.

Pressing the fire button fires a shot at the enemy attack waves, which enter the screen from different edges. The only other movement possible for the player is a diagonal shot, by moving the controller in the opposite direction they want to fire. The game gets gradually harder with waves appearing behind the player or large amounts of enemy shots the player has to avoid.

Having its roots in an arcade game, the objective of Galaxy '93 is to gain the highest possible score. Destroying waves of enemies gives the player points, as well as the bonus rounds considering mostly of cannon fodder-type enemies that occur after clearing a certain number of waves.

452031.overview: Gergundula is a two player only puzzle game much like othello, created as freeware by Axxis in 1992.

452032.overview: A homebrew, single player AMOS game from SCC and CDX in 1994. In the game you must kill all the garden gnomes, all of them. Shoot, shoot, shoot, shoot shoot!

452034.overview:
A freeware puzzle game from Peter Wlceck and Herbert Klackl, created in Modula 2 and released in 1988 in both Assassins CD 02 Ultimate Games and Weird Science! compilation releases.  
 
This program is a simple implementation of the well-known game Master-Mind, in which the aim is to guess a color combination that the computer recognizes as quickly as possible using logical thinking. 

To select a color, you must hover over one the side "paint pots" and then press the left mouse button. The color is automatically placed in the correct place. A color can only appear once in each row. Please note that once a move has been made, it cannot be taken back. 

In the evaluation, the red stones indicate that you have chosen the correct color, a blue stone means that both the color and position of a stone are correct. The position of the evaluation has nothing to do with the position on the field! 
If you want to give up the game, simply click on “Give up”.

452036.overview: A freeware backgammon board game for one or two players, from Marc Fischlin in 1992. Game was written in C. Later versions like 1.3 came out in 1993. The game features saving, multiple colored backgrounds\board graphics. Backgammon is an ancient game that is still as addictive as the day it was invented.  Computerized versions all have the advantage that the loser doesn't have to set up the board or put it away, but what makes this version particularly enjoyable is the fact that it has a number of built-in levels of computer competence. It is suitable for the absolute novice and will continue to be challenging for years to come. Pit your wits against a versatile computer opponent.

452037.overview: A single player asteroids clone by Pow in 1994. Published in Amiga Games Disc & Mag published by CompuTec Verlag in April of 1995.

452038.overview: Pick up all the glowing globs of what I assume is ectoplasm while avoiding floating skills. If you get all the ectoplasm, you move to the next level. Clear all 40 levels and your mission is complete. Simple enough. A shareware platformer from Harald Wagner, released in 1993.

452041.overview: Greeniz is a survival score based shoot 'em up from Black Dragon Design in 1994. It is a fixed screen shooter where you shoot from the left side with spooky green heads coming from the right side of the screen. When you splatter or disable all the heads you can move to the next screen\wave.

452042.overview: Gnosis or Q Game is a Greek-language freeware trivia quiz board game, similar to Trivial Pursuit from L-Soft (Lukas Konias) in 1993. A question editor has been included and the game can save high scores.

452044.overview: Released both as shareware from Thorsten Grosch and as a cover disk (along with Bograts) in Amiga Format magazine, this is an artillery style game where you try to use your limited fuel supply to move your ship and use local gravity to put your shots on one of the 3 enemy target ships before they destroy your 3 ships.

452049.overview:
George's Quest for a Nose is an AMOS based shareware platformer from George Malcolm in 1993. The story behind this platform game is weird, to say the least, but  it boils down to the fact that there are people whose noses have been turned into trumpets, due to being forced to watch too much Coronation Street.  George has escaped and has to find his way to
the  only nose replacement centre which is in Birmingham. Registered version comes with a level editor.

A German-language, text based, shareware soccer\football manager. A new football manager simulation! Become

452053.overview: A freeware text puzzle game written in Modula 2 by Andreas Pahl. The first version was released on June 30th, 1989, the 1.1 version, released in 1992, this game is a simple numeric game. The board - sized 79x23 (one more than standard games) - consists of numbers from 1 to 9. The object of Greed is to erase as much of the screen as possible by moving around   (all 8 directions are allowed in this grid). When you move in a direction,   N   number of grid squares are erased ("eaten") in that direction,   N   being the first number in that direction. Your score reflects the total number of squares "eaten". You may not make a move that places you off the grid or over a previously eaten square. The game is over if there is no more valid moves.

452057.overview:

They are called GOGA and GOGI and are the game heroines respectively. Game hero of an extraordinary environmental game for Amiga computer that is not yet available at this level of and quality and intent. The two are looking for people in GRAY OR GREEN for their fight from 8 to 88 years, who also use a watering can to arm themselves against the ever-increasing environmental destruction underway. GRAY OR GREEN is THE skill game for everyone,a real challenge for for tactical and strategic thinking. The game scenario is about fighting against the GRAY POWER and keeping nature alive.

452062.overview: A freeware, AMOS based game from Marian Schedenig in 1997. A simple, mouse controlled reflex game. You used the mouse to move a puck across the screen while for smaller pucks were moving about and were affected by your puck’s gravity. A round would last as long as you could evade the four small pucks, while your gravitational pull gradually changed over time. The small pucks would bounce at the screen borders, making it rather difficult to keep them under control. In all its simplicity, the game was quite fund to master and brought me some positive feedback from gamers. The game has four levels of difficulty.

452069.overview:
Greed is a simple numeric puzzle game created in AMOS and released as freeware by by Ari Fernelius . The board - sized 79x22 - consists of numbers from 1 to 9. After your start location has been randomly set, you may begin. The task is going through as much of the board as possible, drawing a line (hmm.. or eating the numbers away...). 
 
here are eight directions where to move. Use numeric keyboard keys 1-9 (except "5", which does nothing). Your location will be marked as a flashing cursor. Your cursor will jump forward the number of steps the first number in that direction shows. For example, if the number on the left of your cursor is "5", and you decide to go left (by pressing "4"), the cursor will jump 5 steps to the left, and cover all the numbers on the way with a (blank) line. Drawn line cannot be crossed again - you can only cross a location if there's a number in it.

So watch out where you are going! Avoid going narrow places - if there are not enough small numbers around, you'll be in trouble.

The game ends when you can't move anymore. However, in the end, you will be given the amount of points the distance is to the far most blank line. This is because a couple of other Greeds do so, and I want the scoring system to be exactly the same.

From the far reaches of Neptune, to the safe haven of Earth--battle your way across the Universe in this exciting adventure based on the popular arcade game.

Suspense builds with every beat of thrilling and dramatic music--perhaps unlike any video game music you've ever heard before! To these compelling strains, you'll fend off unremitting waves of spiraling, swirling alien ships. Piloting your spacecraft in a circular flight pattern, blast these fiendish intruders with your rapid-fire lasers--before they vaporize you. And watch out for killer meteors and deadly satellites along the way!

Reach one planet and you'll have just enough time to catch your breath for the next--and more difficult--wave of enemy attacks that separate you from eventually reaching the sanctuary of Earth!

482907.overview: An Amiga game heavily inspired by Galaga in Amiga graphic style. I dreamt of an Amiga shoot 'em up that had to feel arcade-like and could work on the Amiga 1000 with A1050 front-panel 256K expansion or on a stock Amiga 500 with base 512K, something that could be used in shop windows as a showcase of Amiga in 1987. I didn't want a port of Galaga—there already are some ports—I wanted a game that felt 100% Amiga in style and appearance. Also, I know there are some excellent revisitations like Deluxe Galaga (which is a great game, more in the style of a "computer" game), but I wanted a game that makes you feel in the arcades with your freshly acquired Amiga lets say around 1987, but even in late 1985, lol. It nonetheless works on other Amiga models too.
